detail.longDescription: After upgrading macOS, my zsh prompt lost its git status segment and started printing an error on every new prompt. Here is the error: update_current_git_vars:8: bad CPU type in executable: /Users/me/src/zsh-git-prompt/src/.bin/gitstatus I was using the Haskell variant of zsh-git-prompt (olivierverdier/zsh-git-prompt and its forks). My relevant .zshrc lines were: source ~/src/zsh-git-prompt/zshrc.sh GIT_PROMPT_EXECUTABLE='haskell' PROMPT='%(?,%F{green}✔,%F{red}✘%?) %F{green}%n@%m%f:%F{blue}%1~ %f$(git_super_status)%# ' I'm on an Apple Silicon Mac, and the gitstatus binary bundled with this project is precompiled for the wrong CPU architecture, so it can't run. I then tried reinstalling via Homebrew, which produced a related but different error instead: update_current_git_vars:7: no such file or directory: /opt/homebrew/Cellar/zsh-git-prompt/0.5/src/.bin/gitstatus Every fork of zsh-git-prompt I found only actually implements a python and a haskell backend, even though some documentation mentions a "shell" executable option. Setting GIT_PROMPT_EXECUTABLE="shell" did nothing useful in my testing. Is there a maintained alternative that doesn't rely on a precompiled binary at all, so it can't break this way again after a future macOS or architecture change?
